question: Heat and climate: how far above normal was Indonesia's 2025 mean temperature (BMKG)?
finding: National mean air temperature 2025 was 27.05 deg C against a 1991-2020 normal of 26.7 deg C, an anomaly of 0.38 deg C (115 BMKG stations).
unit: deg C anomaly vs 1991-2020 normal (national mean, calendar 2025)
quote: Berdasarkan data dari 115 stasiun pengamatan BMKG, suhu udara rata-rata periode 1991-2020 di Indonesia sebesar 26.7 °C dan suhu udara rata-rata tahun 2025 sebesar 27.05 °C, sehingga anomali suhu udara rata-rata tahun 2025 sebesar 0.38 °C.
gaps: No Jakarta-only temperature series found at BMKG in this run (gap ENV-017).
notes: PESTEL dim: Environmental. Fact only. Interpretation (heat raises cooling load / cold-drink demand) is analysis, not sourced.

question: Heat and climate: where does 2025 rank and was it warmer or cooler than 2024?
finding: 2025 ranks sixth warmest in 1981-2025 (anomaly 0.38 deg C); BMKG states most stations were cooler in 2025 than 2024.
unit: rank among warmest years, 1981-2025 (national)
quote: Sepanjang periode pengamatan tahun 1981 hingga 2025 di Indonesia, tahun 2025 menempati urutan keenam tahun terpanas di Indonesia dengan nilai anomali sebesar 0.38 °C. || ...sebagian besar stasiun pengamatan BMKG bernilai negatif, sehingga dapat disimpulkan bahwa suhu udara rata-rata tahun 2025 relatif lebih dingin dibandingkan tahun 2024.
gaps: The 2024 record year (a BMKG 2024 climate bulletin PDF was found by search but could not be parsed) is not quoted here.
notes: Fact only. Do not read 2025 as a cooling trend; it is one year.

question: Land subsidence: what are Jakarta's current subsidence rates?
finding: DSDA DKI: 2023 geodetic monitoring at 255 GPS points gave an average subsidence of about 4 cm per year, highest at Muara Baru about 10 cm per year; Muara Angke eased from about 7 cm per year in 2023 to about 4.5 cm per year in 2026. DSDA says the trend is slowing in parts of central Jakarta while the north coast stays significant.
unit: cm per year, Jakarta average (2023 survey, 255 GPS points); Muara Baru about 10; Muara Angke about 4.5 (2026)
quote: Berdasarkan hasil pemantauan geodetik pada 255 titik GPS yang dilakukan pada tahun 2023, rata-rata laju penurunan tanah di Jakarta tercatat sekitar 4 sentimeter per tahun. || Pada tahun 2023, laju penurunan tanah di kawasan ini sempat mencapai sekitar 7 sentimeter per tahun. Namun berdasarkan hasil pemantauan terkini pada tahun 2026, angka tersebut menunjukkan perbaikan dan melandai menjadi sekitar 4,5 sentimeter per tahun.
gaps: Next survey scheduled Aug 2026 per the article; result not found. Independent national figures (BRIN, Badan Geologi, Kemenko) seen only in search summaries, not opened.
notes: Values are "sekitar" (approximate). Conflict: a search snippet cited up to 39 cm per year (listrikindonesia.com, not opened); not used. Exposure is concentrated in North Jakarta; whether a site is affected depends on location.

question: Packaging EPR: are cafes and restaurants covered by the producer roadmap Permen LHK P.75/2019 and what is the target?
finding: Yes. Art. 3(3) lists rumah makan, kafe, restoran, jasa boga and hotel as food-and-beverage-service producers; Art. 2 sets a 30% waste reduction target against 2029 waste generation for 2020-2029; Art. 4 covers plastic, aluminium cans, glass and paper packaging that is hard to degrade, recycle or reuse.
unit: % reduction target vs 2029 baseline generation, period 2020-2029
quote: (3) Bidang jasa makanan dan minuman sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) huruf b meliputi: a. rumah makan; b. kafe; c. restoran; d. jasa boga; dan e. hotel. || Peta jalan sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) dilaksanakan untuk mencapai target pengurangan sampah oleh Produsen sebesar 30% (tiga puluh persen) dibandingkan dengan jumlah timbulan Sampah di tahun 2029.
gaps: Whether a new single-outlet foreign-owned cafe must file its own roadmap or only follows via associations (Annex note d allows individual or joint targets) is not settled in the opened text; ask KLHK or a lawyer.
applies_to_entry_mode: own PT PMA; JV in PT PMA; local licensee
notes: The instrument is a ministerial regulation; Annex note e: reporting and evaluation each year. Fact vs analysis: applicability to a small new outlet is analysis.

question: Single-use plastic: what does P.75/2019 Annex say about banned items and when?
finding: Annex I note b: drinking straws, plastic foam food containers, single-use plastic bags and plastic foam are prohibited, effective 1 January 2030. Note c: where a local government bans them earlier, producers must obey the earlier local rule. Annex B.2 (food and beverage services) also lists a ban on single-use plastic cutlery and straws effective 1 Jan 2030.
unit: year the national ban becomes effective (1 January 2030); NOT currently in force
article: Lampiran I, Keterangan b-c; table B.2 row 1a
quote: Terhadap jenis produk, kemasan produk, dan/atau wadah berupa: 1. sedotan plastik; 2. wadah makanan plastik foam; 3. kantong plastik sekali pakai; dan 4. plastik foam, dilarang digunakan, berlaku efektif 1 Januari 2030. || ...dengan waktu yang lebih cepat dari 1 Januari 2030, Produsen wajib menaati kebijakan tersebut
in_force_confirmation: Ban date is in the future (today 2026-10-17): not yet in force. Jakarta rule in ENV-012 is earlier for shopping centres, supermarkets and markets.
amendment_check: No amendment seen on the JDIH record; not exhaustively checked (ENV-011).
gaps: Whether KLHK is preparing a post-2029 or revised rule (a search summary mentions a study) was not opened; check before relying on the 2030 date.
applies_to_entry_mode: own PT PMA; JV in PT PMA; local licensee
notes: Time-limited per lessons rule: the 2030 date is a future effective date. Annex scope wording (B.2 table) partly garbled in text extraction; the Keterangan b text above was read clean.

question: Jakarta plastic-bag ban: who is bound and what is allowed?
finding: Pergub DKI 142/2019: managers of shopping centres, supermarkets/minimarkets and traditional markets must use reusable "eco-friendly" bags and may not use single-use plastic shopping bags (Art. 5); shopping-centre managers must impose this on every tenant (Art. 6(1)(a)-(b)); supermarkets must sell reusable bags near the till, not free (Art. 9(1)(b)); tenants may still give single-use plastic packaging bags for unwrapped food, until a greener alternative exists (Art. 7).
unit: qualitative rule
quote: Pengelola Pusat Perbelanjaan, Toko Swalayan, dan Pasar Rakyat wajib menggunakan Kantong Belanja Ramah Lingkungan. || Pelaku Usaha di Pusat Perbelanjaan dapat menyediakan Kantong Kemasan Plastik Sekali Pakai. (2) ... hanya dapat digunakan untuk mewadahi bahan Pangan yang belum terselubung kemasan apapun.
